title: quiet-echoes-field-walk-notes-and-feature-sketches-2026-03-11
content:
Purpose: quick capture from 3day field-walks (Mar 8–10) with 7 customers — aim was to listen for low-signal, high-friction behaviors that don’t show up in telemetry. This doc is intentionally rough: quotes, micro-ideas, and immediate low-effort probes engineers could try in the next sprint.

High level theme: quiet failure modes around inference economics + UX transparency
- Customers generally see model regressions as a "cost problem" not purely quality: when generation costs spike (longer token chains or repeated re-tries) product teams treat it as an infrastructure issue and throttle UX (shorter answers, disable streaming) rather than tune prompts or model variants.
- Small, persistent friction: users prune prompts radically to avoid token costs which reduces usefulness. Customers asked for visibility (per-route cost counter) and safe fallbacks that preserve signal.

Representative customer quotes (raw):
- "We turned off streaming for low-tier users because it was eating our budget overnight." — fintech benchmark client
- "Sometimes the model gives good but expensive answers; other times cheap answers are fine. We want control per route, not per-account." — e-commerce search team
- "KV cache misses are the silent killer — 3x token cost in spikes and we only saw it in billing after the fact." — enterprise platform team

Observed patterns + quick telemetry notes:
- Correlation: increased token counts + KV cache invalidations after model upgrades (noticed in Canary @region-us-west).
- Behavioral signal: customers circumvented rate limits by batching client-side; this increases tail latency and creates hot shards.
- Ops note: a customer reported highest cost windows at 02:00–04:00 UTC (automated nightly jobs hitting endpoints).

Microfeature proposals (ranked by effort -> impact)
1) Per-route visible budget and recent cost histogram (UX + small backend counter) — low effort, immediate de-risk. Rationale: gives product owners a lever and visibility to adjust.
   - Mock: small banner in Console: "Route budget this month: 73% used; median cost/resp: 315 tokens"
   - Owner: Product Console (Priya) + telemetry eng (Owen)

2) Canary KV-cache telemetry flag (expose cache hit/miss ratio per model variant + route) — medium effort, high signal for ops and SRE.
   - Purpose: detect spike windows tied to cache warming/invalidations.
   - Quick probe: enable for three high-volume tenants for 2 weeks.

3) Model-variant suggestion overlay (Console): surface cheaper compatible variants with estimated cost delta and small sample outputs.
   - UX: "Switch to 4-bit quantized variant — expected cost -42% with similar quality for short answers"
   - Risk: sample mismatch; require offline eval harness.

4) Auto-fallback transparency in API (opt-in): return explicit fallback reason code when system routes to cheaper variant (e.g., capacity, cost policy).
   - Benefit: reduces confusion and helps clients decide to retry or accept cheaper answer.

Low-effort runtime patches / experiments
- Enable prefix caching for routes with high repetition (simple config flag per-route). Test on two customers who have repetitive system prompts.
- Short-term quota alerting: add an "unexpected cost spike" webhook that fires when per-route spend > 200% of trailing 7-day median.
- A/B for streaming toggle placement: move control to per-route defaults (not account-level) and measure churn in streaming-enabled sessions.

Customer-specific asks (actionable)
- Fintech client: wants a way to "pin model versions" and a transparent estimate of cost before rollout. Suggested: pre-rollout estimate tool in Console + canary tokens.
- Marketplace customer: requests a route-level "quality preset" slider (concise | balanced | thorough) that maps to model + length budget.
- Enterprise platform: wants a KV cache warmup API (pre-warm cache for expected sessions) and better logs when cache invalidates.

Open questions / concerns to surface to Eng + Product:
- How strong is model-variant compatibility across common prompt patterns? Need small eval set per customer to avoid quality regressions if surfaced as suggestion.
- Cost transparency tradeoffs: how much extra telemetry (and storage) do we accept to compute per-route cost histograms?
- Can we safely expose cache hit/miss ratios without leaking sensitive usage patterns? (privacy requests from regulated customers)

Suggested immediate next steps (next 2 weeks)
- Product + CS: run a 1-hour "walkthrough" with the fintech and enterprise platform customers to validate the per-route budget mock (Priya + Maya).
- Eng: enable KV-cache telemetry flag for three tenants and collect 2 weeks of data (Owen). Add quick dashboard in Grafana.
- Growth/Support: prepare a short explainer for customers on "cost-aware defaults" and recommended guardrails (2 page PDF).

Appendix: quick sketches and links
- Sketch links: Confluence:CS/field-walks/q1-2026 (see attached)
- Quick Jira tickets to spin up: CS-4872 (per-route budget UI), CS-4873 (KV-cache telemetry flag), CS-4874 (cost spike webhook)

Notes to self: keep follow-ups lightweight and experiment-driven. This cluster of signals feels different from blunt latency complaints — it's about economics shaping product decisions. If we fix visibility (low-hanging), many downstream breakages go away.
